memos.risk:
Risk officer read on SPLURGE: I'd refuse. Several flags stack up. Drawdown is 64% from the 30-minute high, with 30-minute return at -57%. Bundle share is 84%, which points to coordinated buying rather than organic demand. Sell-to-buy ratio was 1.27 in the first two minutes after graduation, and the launch bot was present. Pool depth is only 46.9 SOL, so a $20 round trip faces heavy slippage, and the last 15 minutes show sellers outnumbering the net flow.

If the desk overrides and buys anyway, the most I'd allow is a $5 ticket, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. Any move up should be taken quickly, not held.

Refuse any size if the bundle share stays above roughly 50%, if pool depth stays under about 50 SOL, or if the sell-to-buy ratio keeps running above 1. Skipping costs nothing; this profile fits the losing base rates.
memos.scout:
Honest case for buying SPLURGE now is weak. The strongest point is the last 15 minutes: buy volume of 42 SOL from 104 buyers, net flow of +4.5 SOL, and a +17% return off recent lows, so some fresh demand is present. Organic classification, no airdrop dump, a modest top-3 concentration (10.9%), and a reasonable 47 SOL pool are also in its favor.

But the case breaks down quickly. The curve shows 84% bundle share and the first two minutes after graduation had a 1.27 sell-to-buy ratio, which points to coordinated early activity rather than broad demand. The coin is still down 64% from its 30-minute high and 57% over the window, and the last 15 minutes saw 94 sellers against 104 buyers with sells nearly matching buys. A 17% bounce inside a deep drawdown is the pattern that usually fails to hold. Against a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a base rate of roughly 20% losses on random post-graduation buys, I can't find a case that real demand will persist for the next 30-60 minutes.

Recommendation: skip.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: a slow bleed plus fee drag, not a clean rug. The coin is already down 56.6% over 30 minutes and sits 64% below its 30-minute high. The last 15 minutes show sellers dominating: sell SOL of 37.5 against buy SOL of 42.0, with 94 sellers versus 104 buyers, and a net inflow of only 4.5 SOL. That is distribution into a thin pool (46.9 SOL depth), so any bounce gets sold into.

The curve data is a warning sign: 84% bundle share and a completer share near 40% suggest coordinated early buying, so bundled holders may be exiting. The launch bot present and a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.27 right after graduation point the same way.

A bounce of 5% would be eaten by the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, and the trend is down. Skip.
